result.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
result.summary: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. We illustrate this with a textbook theorem whose hypothesis is more restrictive than asserted. We invite the inverse problems community to extend and build on the library.

AI.brief_summary: 论文介绍 AutoIP：一个由 AI agent 自动形式化的 Lean 库，覆盖经典线性正则化理论及其所依赖的泛函分析；作者主张把人的精力放在核对形式陈述是否符合自然语言原意而非检查证明，并给出陈述级自动测试可暴露已有文献中假设过强问题的例子。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证明已被机器检查、风险转移到陈述是否忠实于意图」的结构，可能与 LVR 中「答案正确但内部 latent 是否真正承载视觉证据」的忠实性核查相通；陈述层面的低成本自动测试思路可供核查是否用于 latent 内容与答案贡献分配的评价设计。
